handling.guidance: One reading, said at a moment: what holds the person's attention now, not a record of a period. topic is one agreed spelling per subject, lower case with words joined by hyphens (deskcam, never DeskCam or desk cam), the way health.medication.dose fixes the drug's spelling, so a query can match it exactly; the store never reads inside a note. intensity is a whole number from 1 to 5. at is the minute it was said, as a wall clock in Australia/Sydney or at the offset source_time names; a reading about an earlier time is dated at that time, and note says how it was worked out. The id is declared in identity_template, <source>:attention/<topic>/<at as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM>, then source_time's offset (+11:00), so one minute in two zones is two readings, and every writer builds it from there: leave id out and Anam fills it; send it and it must match. Two readings of one topic in one minute are one reading. How long a topic held the person is the mind.attention.started and mind.attention.ended pair, which the person declares; readings never open or close it.
handling.label: {/topic}

schema.description: One self-reported attention reading: at a moment the person says what is absorbing them (the topic) and how strongly, from 1 to 5. Said by the person as it happens, through a conversation or the Workbench. It records what the person said, not what anything else infers. Version 2 adds handling.label, a short label a page draws a row as, every rule unchanged.

at.description: When the person said it, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM as a wall clock in Australia/Sydney, or at the offset source_time names. This is the fact time.

intensity.description: How strongly the topic held the person's attention at that moment, a whole number from 1 (a passing interest) to 5 (nothing else existed).

topic.description: What the attention is on, in one agreed spelling: lower case, words joined by hyphens, the way a drug has one spelling. A project, a subject or an activity, named as the person already names it, so the same thing is always the same string.

id.description: Identity, composed from the rest by the Definition's identity_template: the source prefix, then attention, the topic and the moment, then the offset source_time names. A writer may leave it out and Anam fills it; one that sends it must send exactly the composition.

note.description: Free text in the person's words, about what is absorbing them.

source_time.description: How `at` was read: value is the wall clock as the person said it, zone the zone it was said in (an IANA name when the writer knows one, else the offset again), offset the offset from UTC it had then, and basis who decided the zone (source when the person's own client or browser names it, configuration when the writer's setting does). The fact time is `at` read at offset.

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

offset.description: The offset from UTC value had at that moment in zone, +HH:MM or -HH:MM, which names one instant even in an hour the zone repeats. A writer that cannot tell it refuses rather than guess.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.
